purpose: The frozen holdout of the returns preregistration (PREREGISTRATION.md, committed 46a4005d). Every candidate the search recorded, with both readings, the readings of each instant used and left open, T with its terms, and every exclusion with its reason. No engine result for a holdout candidate is in this file or was computed before it was committed.

decisions.decision: A real native whom the source does not name but specifies by birth data or by the radical longitude meets W1, as a hypothetical native the source fully specifies would. W7 still applies: born before 1900, or a cited death record, or hypothetical.

decisions.rule: The fixtures and how each runs; W5
decisions.decision: When the work states the birth instant in a passage the return refers to (the same serial or book), the fixture is whole-chain, so W5 applies to the birth as well.

The radical longitude counts as used in the working when a working the passage prints for that native uses it, or when the passage states that the native's return is to that printed value; it then counts for each of that native's returns in the passage, with that printing's unit. A return figure that shows the body at the natal value is not counted: it shows the working's result at the figure's precision, not the radical the working used. (Revised before the freeze after the independent review: the first version also counted such figures.)

decisions.rule: The reading of each instant; the tolerance, b; the cap
decisions.decision: A return whose time basis is open (not stated, and not fixed by a rule the author states) and whose place is neither printed nor fixed by a rule the author states cannot be read under b, since local mean time and the civil time in force need a place. T is then unbounded and the candidate is recorded as too imprecise to test.

A day and month printed with the instant, with the year fixed by the passage (for example "the present year" in a dated note, or a sentence naming the year of the figure), meets W2. A clock time printed with no day or month does not.

A printed logarithm that is not the logarithm of the printed figure it stands for is a source slip when the instant then does not follow from the printed figures by more than its last printed unit. Rounding the author does openly in the working (taking the nearest tabulated logarithm, or a figure to the minute) is the author's working, and the check uses it as printed.

T.L.T. ("true local time") in American Astrology is local mean time at the printed longitude: the series derives it from G.M.T. at 4 minutes per degree. Where both are printed for an instant, G.M.T. is the reading used, since the working finds it first; the two agree by construction.

Times printed as hours.minutes with single-digit minutes ("2.0 p.m.", "2.3 p.m.", "0.5 p.m.") are read as hours and minutes, the notation both readers found the source using for its other times. Their unit is the minute.
When the place is not in GeoNames cities15000 (the site's committed index), the nearest listed town stands for it, with the same plus or minus 0.1 degree reading of the longitude.

A converse (prenatal) return, the instant before the birth when the body stands at its radical longitude, is not a return of the body to its radical longitude in W2's sense: the body returns to that longitude only after the radical instant. Converse returns are recorded and excluded.

A departure from W6 and S6, made before any run and disclosed: a scan counts as public only when a library, archive or digitization project makes it openly available (for example archive.org's library and periodical collections, the Digital Library of India, IAPSOP, Google Books full view). An individual's upload of a work still in copyright to archive.org's community collections ("opensource", "community", "magazine_packs") is not counted, and the evidence does not point to it. The line is drawn by provenance, so the Digital Library of India scans of the 1933 and 1942 works behind seven scored fixtures are counted. The excluded records keep their ids and dates; their readings, natives, authors and titles are withheld from holdout.json, holdout-planetary.json and search-log.json, after the owner's private-birth-data check of 8 November 2026.
decisions.reason: The evidence should not rest on, or send readers to, copies of in-copyright works that individuals uploaded without evident permission. W6 and S6 as written do not draw this line, so it is recorded as a departure rather than a reading.
decisions.effect: Excludes 31 records (F5-02, F5-09 to F5-30, F5-34 to F5-37, F5-43 to F5-46), every post-1960 source the F5 brief named. On their first readings, at least two book records and up to five records of one serial look eligible under the cap; none was read a second time. These are modern computed returns, which would more likely agree with the engine than not, so the departure does not look chosen to help a pass.

decisions.decision: An instant printed with a bare trailing figure and no unit mark ("10h 42m 3 p.m.") is read to the last marked unit, the minute, with r for the minute (30 s), which covers both readings of the figure (3 s or 0.3 minute).

When two searchers found and read the same passage independently, each reading is the other's blind second reading, and the passage is one candidate (recorded once, under the earlier id; the other id is recorded as a duplicate).

When the source prints two different birth instants for the native and does not say which one its return was computed from, the birth reading is open by their difference, which the tolerance's b takes as dB; where that alone exceeds the cap, the candidate is recorded as too imprecise to test.

S8 checks the working that gives the printed return instant, from the printed figures it starts from, the radical as printed included. A slip found in a separate natal computation that produced the radical is recorded with the fixture and is not used to exclude it.
applies: F3-18 (the natal Sun's own working, p. 90, gives 7' 42.2" where 7' 40" is printed, so 11 24 13 for the printed 11 24 11; carried through the return working the instant would be 8 h 6.6 m against the printed 8 h 5 m)
F3-11 (the misprinted intermediate 25' 33" is not used by the proportion, which follows from the printed inputs; F3-11 is excluded by the cap instead)

decisions.decision: A radical printed in the working with trailing zero seconds ("13° 55' 00"") that the source also prints to the arc-minute is read to the arc-minute, as both readers read it.

A departure from S3, disclosed: candidates excluded on facts that no reading of the page changes were read once, not twice. These are births before 1800 known from history (W5: F2-07, F3-08, F4-C11, F4-C28, F4-C39), the post-1900 births of unnamed natives (W7: F4-C22, F5-01, F5-03, F5-07, F5-08; the exclusion protects their privacy whatever a second reading found), and community uploads (W6, D11). F2-05 (an event chart, W1) was read twice.
H5 orders a work's fixtures by publication date, then by page, then by printed order on the page (the order of the candidates' ids within a passage, which follows the print).

Fig. XVIII, Map for June 2, 1893 (p. 105), prints cusps and positions to the arc-minute and the date only. Passage-level: (1) Pages 108-111 (leaves 0102-0105) lie between the two cited ranges and outside the citation. They print Art. 81, Solar Return to the Progressed Sun (Problems 47-49: the Sun's return to its progressed longitude, with instants on 30 June 1893, 17 July 1909 and 18 July 1910), and Arts. 82-83 with Problems 50-52, current synodical lunations. No entries are recorded for them. (2) The instant at the top of p. 112 (October 13, 1910, 3-57 a.m. G.M.T.) ends Problem 52, a synodic lunation, not a return. (3) p. 103 holds the end of the synodic-lunation Problems 42-43 and the opening of Art. 80, with no return instant. (4) Art. 80 says the Sun's radical must be taken to the second of arc or a tenth, since one minute of arc gives about 24 minutes of time. (5) The native was born in 1865. (6) p. 1 also gives a second, exercise nativity (12° 59′ N, 5 h 21 m E, 8 41 A.M. L.M.T., December 13, 1871), for which no return is worked on the cited pages. s8.note: Each step follows from its own inputs: 11°33′7″ - 10°33′55″ = 59′12″; 11°24′11″ - 10°33′35″ = 50′36″; 24 h x 50′36″/59′12″ = 20h 30.81m (20h 30m 49s), printed 20 hours 31 mins.; the printed logarithms are those of their figures (59′12″: 0.482951, a.c. 9.517049; 50′36″: 0.551122; 24: 0.875061); their sum is 10.94323, printed 0.94323, which gives 20h 30.82m; noon of 31st March + 20h 31m = 8h 31m A.M. of 1st April; + 5h 25m = 1h 56m P.M.; S.T. 0 38 31 + 1 56 0 + 0 0 20 = 2 34 51. BUT the noon longitude of 31st March is used with two values: 10°33′55″ (as first printed; it gives the motion 59′12″) and 10°33′35″ (in the subtraction that gives 50′36″). From the figures as first printed (10°33′55″ throughout) the difference is 50′16″ and the proportion gives 20h 22.70m, i.e. 8h 22.7m A.M. of 1st April, 8.3 minutes before the printed 8-31 A.M., more than its last printed unit (1 minute). With 10°33′35″ throughout (motion 59′32″) it gives 20h 23.92m, i.e. 8h 23.9m A.M. Also printed: '50′ 36°' with a degree sign where 50′ 36″ is meant (repeated as 50′ 36″ in the next sentence), and an asterisked 'Corrn.' with no footnote on pp. 281-282.

firstReading.native: Léon Gambetta ('Gambetta'). P. 99 text: dies between 44 and 45 years '(31 déc. 1882)'.
firstReading.birth_as_printed: Natal figure p. 95 (printed sideways; leaf 112): 'Gambetta - Cahors - 2 avril 1838 - 8h soir'; 'lambda = 44°27' (N)'; 'RA MC = 130°23''; Sun: RA 11°37', declination 4°59'. P. 19 (leaf 36): 'Cahors le 2 avril 1838, à 8 h. du soir', latitude of Cahors 44°27' nord. P. 16 (leaf 33): sidereal time 'à vue 8 h. 41 m. 32 s.', taking 8 h as Cahors local time and neglecting the Greenwich-Cahors meridian difference; MC 8° Leo, As 1° Scorpio.
firstReading.radical_longitude_as_printed: Sun '12°38' du Bélier' (p. 72 text, leaf 89); natal figure p. 95 prints the Sun as '12.38'.
firstReading.return_instant_as_printed: Figure caption p. 99: 'Révolution solaire du 2 avril 1869 - 8h 25m matin'. Sun in the figure '12.38'; MC 14 Aquarius, As 11 Gemini. The figures are handwritten (the author's 'dessins'), drawn for the birthplace (p. 72).
firstReading.time_basis: Not stated for the revolution figures. Rules the author states: p. 72, the solar revolution is the sky 'au lieu de naissance' for the precise moment of the anniversary when the Sun returns to its exact natal longitude, the hour being computed from that year's ephemeris, 'date et heure pouvant être différentes de celles de la naissance, par suite des conventions admises pour la mesure du temps'. Supplement pp. 169-170: Raphael's ephemeris positions are for Greenwich mean noon; the RA of MC is computed with the local time of the birthplace and the planets' longitudes for the corresponding Greenwich time (worked example: Berlin, 3 June 1867, 4 h soir); 'Heure de naissance: c'est l'heure locale du temps moyen'; since 1891 Paris mean time is legal time; the Sun's longitude must be computed as exactly as possible to set up solar revolutions. P. 16 (Gambetta's natal figure): 8 h taken as the local hour of Cahors, neglecting the difference between the Greenwich and Cahors meridians.
firstReading.units_and_truncation: Return instant to the minute (handwritten h and m). Birth time to the hour ("8h soir"). Sun to the arc-minute (12.38). Other figure positions to the arc-minute; declinations to the arc-minute. No truncation stated.
firstReading.ephemeris_and_interpolation: Raphael's ephemeris ('éphémérides de Raphaël', pp. 16, 22-23, 169-170; Greenwich mean noon; the book reproduces the November 1837 pages as an example). Interpolation for the returns: not stated.
firstReading.working_printed: No working printed for the return: the figure only (caption, cusps, planets, declinations).
firstReading.place_longitude_printed: No. The natal figures print only the latitude (lambda); no longitude of any example's birthplace is printed (the supplement's Berlin example prints Berlin's and Greenwich's longitudes from Paris).

firstReading.return_instant_as_printed: Fig. 3 caption: 'RÉVOLUTION SOLAIRE du 24 AOUT 1831 (3 h. 50 MATIN)'. Sun in the figure '0°11' (11.25)'; As 15 Leo, MC 1 Taurus (as drawn). Text (p. 149): the revolution solaire of 1831 'régissant la soixante-troisième année (celle de la mort)'; 'La figure 3 donne celle de l'anniversaire de 1831'.
firstReading.time_basis: Not stated for the revolution. Rules in the same issue ('Note sur l'emploi des éphémérides de Raphaël', P. Flambart, pp. 198-200): the birth hour is 'en principe l'heure locale'; planetary longitudes are interpolated for the corresponding Greenwich time (example: Gambetta, 7 h 54 m soir Greenwich for 8 h Cahors); older French works count longitude from Paris, 0 h 9 m 20 s east of Greenwich.
firstReading.units_and_truncation: Return instant to the minute; birth time to the hour ('quatre heures du matin'); Sun to the arc-minute; declinations to the arc-minute. No truncation stated.
firstReading.ephemeris_and_interpolation: Raphael's ephemeris (Greenwich mean noon) and 'un calcul très simple de proportion' (linear interpolation) per the same issue's note; not restated for this return.
firstReading.working_printed: No working: figure only.
firstReading.place_longitude_printed: No.
firstReading.death_record: Born before 1900; no death record needed under W7.
firstReading.eligibility_notes: Serial not in ineligible.json. FLAG W5: the native was born in 1769, before 1800; a source stating the birth gives a whole-chain fixture, whose birth must also lie in 1800-2026. Recorded so the exclusion can be logged.

firstReading.native: Ernest Legouvé (académicien)

Figure 1 (p. 149, natal chart) has handwritten captions, mostly illegible at the scan's resolution; its top-left note reads 'Domific. mod. ... / Éphémérides de Raphaël'
firstReading.return_instant_as_printed: p. 149: 'au moment où le Soleil retournait à sa Longitude radicale le 15 février 1903, à 3 h. 27 m. 28 s., temps astronomique moyen à Paris'. Figure 2 caption (p. 153, handwritten, partly legible) appears to repeat '1903 - 15 févr. 3h 27m 28s T.A. m.'
firstReading.time_basis: Return: 'temps astronomique moyen à Paris' (Paris mean time, astronomical reckoning, day beginning at noon), stated. Birth: '8 heures du matin', basis not stated
firstReading.units_and_truncation: Return to the second; birth to the hour ('8 heures'); footnote angles to 0.1 arc-second; no truncation stated
firstReading.ephemeris_and_interpolation: Figure 1 names 'Éphémérides de Raphaël' (for the natal chart); not stated for the revolution
firstReading.working_printed: partly: footnote p. 150 gives the revolution chart's figures: 'L'Asc. Dr. du MC^R étant = 16°19'7".5, celle du Soleil 328°2'26", la Dist. du MC au Soleil = 48°16'41".5. Son demi-arc diurne étant égal à 74°46'10", le Soleil est à 25°29'28".5 de distance de l'horizon occidental; et le tiers de son demi-arc étant = 24°55'23", il est donc en VIII à 34'5" de la Pointe.' (the revolution's RAMC 16°19'7".5 is printed; the return instant itself is not derived)
firstReading.ampm_or_civil_day: Return: astronomical time stated; birth: 'du matin'
firstReading.place_longitude_printed: no (Paris named only)
firstReading.death_record: born before 1900 (the article: died 14 March 1903)
firstReading.other_notes: Whole-chain. Not in ineligible.json. Overlaps family F4 (French periodical, before 1960); recorded here because the same article holds a lunar return (F5-32)

firstReading.units_and_truncation: Return to the second (G.M.T. and L.M.T.); radical longitude to 0.1 arc-second; birth to the minute; no truncation stated
firstReading.other_notes: Whole-chain (birth date, time and place printed) with the radical longitude also printed. The book's 'standard nativity' and 'returns to the progressed Sun' (Problems 47-49) are not returns to the radical longitude; Problem 44 (George V's 1893 solar return, 7-53-52 p.m. G.M.T., June 2, 1893) is a development return (H3) and is not recorded
